ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the primary coil of an ideal transformer, marked with number of turns n1; in the circuit at the upper end of the primary coil, ammeter A1 is connected in series, and the voltmeter V on the left side is connected between the two ends a and b, in parallel with the input end of the primary coil. For an ideal transformer, the input power equals the output power, so P1=U1I1=220×0.2=44 W. The secondary-coil load is a pure resistor R=44 Ω, therefore P2=U2^2/R, giving U2=sqrt(P2R)=sqrt(44×44)=44 V. For an ideal transformer, the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, so n1:n2=U1:U2=220:44=5:1.
